reasons: Only the setup section of this file was provided, so most of its behaviour cannot be checked.

terms.meaning: A supporting slide placed at the end of the deck with detailed data.
A colour category (red, amber, or grey) used to show how serious a delay or overrun is.

sections.name: File setup, Tone
sections.title: Imports, colours and the no-invented-cause rule
sections.what: Sets up the imports for colours, the slide frame, the cited-value display, the citation hook, and the project helpers. Defines the three tone categories and states that the reasons column never invents a cause.
sections.why: The header comment records this rule as the reason for the no-cause note.
sections.watch_out: The tone colours are used later in the file, so they must match the colour definitions the rest of the file expects, which cannot be confirmed from this section.

sections.name: classifyDelay
sections.title: Delay type label for each project
sections.what: Gives each project one short label: Cancelled, Dropped, Cost + Schedule, Cost, Schedule, or None. Stopped-status words are checked first, then cost and schedule overruns.
sections.why: The Delay type column needs one label per row. The order of the checks suggests a stopped project keeps its stopped label even if it also overran.
sections.watch_out: The words that count as Dropped here differ from the bubble chart: postponed and suspended projects show as Dropped in this table but as On hold in the bubble chart.

sections.name: TONE_STYLE
sections.title: Colours for delay tags
sections.what: Picks the background and text colour for each delay tag. Cancelled, dropped and cost-plus-schedule use red, a single overrun uses amber, and no overrun uses grey.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the names, which point to the shared status colours used elsewhere in the app.
sections.watch_out: A new tone name must be added to this lookup, or its tags will have no colours.

sections.name: ReasonsSlide (part 1)
sections.title: Reasons table heading and citation helper
sections.what: Builds the appendix slide frame and the table headings: Project, Delay type, and Reason(s) for the delay. It also sets up the Full citation action, which opens the complete evidence for one project and field in a side drawer. The header shows how many projects are included.
sections.why: Lets a reader check the exact evidence behind each stated reason instead of relying on a short summary.
sections.watch_out: The field names passed to the drawer must match the evidence paths in scanFields.ts, which is not in this packet. A mismatch opens the wrong or empty evidence.

sections.name: ReasonsSlide (part 2)
sections.title: Reason lines and status for each row
sections.what: For each project, shows a cost reason line, a schedule reason line, and a status line when they apply. A line appears when there is an overrun or a stated reason, and the status line appears for stopped projects. If nothing applies, the row says no cost or schedule overrun was recorded.
sections.why: Keeps each row short while showing only the reasons that matter for that project.
sections.watch_out: A stated reason alone makes its line appear even when the project shows no overrun, so a row can show a reason next to a None label.

summary: Appendix slide that lists, for each project, the stated reason for its cost or schedule failure, or says that no cause is given in public sources.
purpose: Shows the causes recorded in the scan data without adding any cause that is not there.
why: The header comment says the reasons column never invents a cause and shows a muted note when none is stated.
how: Reading the visible notes: the slide imports colours, the frame, the cited-value component, the citation hook, and the project helpers. For each project it shows the cost or schedule reason from the data when present, and the muted no-cause note when absent. The remaining steps are in sections that were not provided.
inputs: The slide context (`ctx`) and each project's status, cost, schedule, and reason fields, read through the project helpers.
outputs: An appendix table inside the House frame, with the reasons column coloured by tone.
risks: Only the setup section was provided, so the table logic and reason handling are not verified. The reason text comes from the data and is not checked here.
debug: If a reason is missing, check the source field in the scan data and the cited-value display. If the colour tone looks wrong, check the tone mapping in the file.
